description: This file contains build definitions, variable assignments, and macros for building firmware images for Sercomm devices, including script invocations, image partitioning, cryptography, and device-specific configurations.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-append-tail
methods.description: Appends a tail pattern to the device image, writing specific bytes at a certain offset.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-crypto
methods.description: Performs cryptographic processing on the input file, including encryption and hashing.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-factory-cpj
methods.description: Creates device-specific firmware components using headers, kernel, and root filesystem offsets.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-factory-cqr
methods.description: Creates partition data for firmware using device identifiers and image size.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-kernel
methods.description: Builds kernel image with header and appends kernel data.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-kernel-factory
methods.description: Creates kernel headers for multiple kernel images with specified offsets.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-mkhash
methods.description: Generates and embeds a hash value into the firmware image.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-part-tag
methods.description: Adds partition tagging to a specific file.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-part-tag-common
methods.description: Adds a partition tag to a specified file using a script.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-payload
methods.description: Creates a payload with device identifiers, cryptography, and additional padding.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-pid-setbit
methods.description: Sets a specific bit in the firmware image at a given offset.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-prepend-tagged-kernel
methods.description: Prepends a tagged kernel to an existing kernel image.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-reset-slot1-chksum
methods.description: Resets checksum in the image at a specified offset.

methods.name: Build/sercomm-sysupgrade-cpj
methods.description: Creates a sysupgrade image for CPJ devices with proper headers and root filesystem.
